evidence.title: Excited to share that Jalaj and I are building Intelligence Factory and we're backed by Y Combinator and Comma Capital
evidence.text:
Excited to share that Jalaj and I are building Intelligence Factory and we're backed by Y Combinator and Comma Capital.

Robotics is the new paradigm. With hardware converging, Intelligence is the biggest bottleneck. Our world was built for humans and we're giving robots the ability to reason and act like us.

The way we learn any task - by seeing, doing, and feeling - is how we train robots. We're building general intelligence that works on any robot and fits seamlessly within our world.

In the coming weeks, we will share more about our approach as we deploy across manufacturing, warehousing, and retail. Stay tuned!

We'd like to thank Pete Koomen, Max Kolysh, David Ongchoco, Adarsh Bhatt, Allen Gannett, Julien Pache and Wilson Lin for their support

evidence.title: Robots won't fail because they can't see - they will fail because they can't feel
evidence.text:
Robots won't fail because they can't see - they will fail because they can't feel.

The sense of touch allows us to differentiate between picking up a plastic wrapper and a phone. It's the reason we're able to work with objects of all shapes, sizes, and structures. Without this information, robots are operating blind in the physical world.

At Intelligence Factory, Jalaj Shukla and Julien Stocker are building data collection hardware that captures force and tactile feedback from human demonstrations. With this, our models generalize across a wide range of objects.

If you're an engineer passionate about robotic intelligence and want to help solve this, reach out.

evidence.title: $10B has been invested in robotics, but very little of this technology has reached the customer
evidence.text:
$10B has been invested in robotics, but very little of this technology has reached the customer.

Most robots in the market break with any variation in the environment.

In the real world, robots don't compete with other robots - they compete with humans. And no business pays for a robot that works 80% of the time when their current system works 100% of the time. This is the deployment gap.

The standard fix is a data flywheel: deploy, collect data, retrain, redeploy. But this is slow, expensive, and doesn't work in practice.

At Intelligence Factory, we're making this flywheel dramatically faster. We're soon deploying with customers in warehouses, grocery and data centers.

evidence.title: When I was a kid in India, I had this wish
evidence.text:
When I was a kid in India, I had this wish.

Not a plan. Not a roadmap. Just a quiet, almost embarrassing wish that one day I would have my own company in Silicon Valley, building something that actually matters to me and to the community.

I did not know how. I just knew I had to keep going.

While at University of Pennsylvania there were a lot of times I tried pitching some half-baked idea at The Wharton School, pitching auto-generated sign language captions for YouTube videos Jerome Fisher M&T Program, working with my entrepreneurship professor (Tom Cassel) not really knowing what I was doing. I just knew what I wished for and tried my best in whatever I was doing. I didn't know what I was preparing for. Even in my most rational moments, I would not have imagined what I'd be doing two years down the line, or that it would even be possible.

I just kept doing my best, whether it was an assignment for a course I didn't care about or a random job at a company that felt unrelated to everything. Things just quietly add up. The dots were connecting. I just couldn't see it yet.

Today, Yash Sinha and I are building Intelligence Factory, general intelligence for robots, backed by Y Combinator, Comma Capital, and Allen Gannett. And standing here, I finally see all the dots.
But this moment is not mine alone. It belongs to every person in these photos.

- My mentors Nadia Figueroa, Kostas Daniilidis, Ho Jin Choi, Shafagh Keyvanian, Dr. Kirankumar Rushinath jagtap, Ted Solomon who saw something in me before I did.
- My friends, Pratyush Mallick, Sai Chand Gubbala, Manas Kulkarni Yadnik Bendale, Harsh Yellai, Santosh Yerramsetty, Richal Abhang, Irene Grace Karot Polson who never let me shrink.
- My family, Palashi Singhal, Aditya Rajeev, Saurav Agrawal, Hardik Shukla, Archis Basangar,Manish Raul ,Mrunal Deshmukh, Radhika Prayage, Devansh Shukla who sacrificed quietly so I could dream loudly.

This is not my achievement. This is our cumulative effort.

I want to build this the right way; honest, ethical, human. A place where people do meaningful work and go home fulfilled. That's the bigger dream now. And I need you now more than ever !!!

dreams · courage · hope · prayers · family · friends · love · serendipity · gratitude · joy · bliss

We started Intelligence Factory with only one goal - deploy robots in the real world. We are more excited than ever to make this a reality.

evidence.title: Excited to share a big update - I started a company and got into Y Combinator
evidence.text:
Excited to share a big update - I started a company and got into Y Combinator!

After an incredible year and a half leading GTM at Clipbook, I'm returning to a space I've loved since Mr. Rucker's 8th grade history class: government, politics, and now, how AI will change the way the private sector interacts with our public institutions.

I'll be sharing more soon but for now: we already have our first few partners and have helped them achieve real results, all with a growing pipeline of amazing companies.

We've also started building our early engineering and policy teams. If you're excited by AI and helping ambitious companies advance the national interest, please reach out!
